primary.thesis: None of the four coins reaches $1B FDV by Dec 25, 2026, so C5 (None) resolves YES and every coin-specific contract resolves NO. The mechanism is simple. All four are memecoins. Three are on Robinhood Chain, a new chain whose liquidity and trader base are still small. The fourth, ANSEM, is a pump.fun Solana token whose appeal rests on one influencer's name. The task gives no current FDVs, but a coin that trades under a Polymarket 'first to $1B' ladder is almost certainly far below the line, likely somewhere in the tens of millions. Getting to $1B in under three months would take a 10-100x move. Few memecoins in history have done that, and it needs a broad memecoin mania with fresh retail money flowing in. The rules do count a brief wick on CoinGecko or CoinMarketCap, and fixed-supply memecoins make FDV equal to market cap, which is some risk. But thin liquidity makes the move hard to sustain, and even a momentary print still needs a lot of real buying.

basket.reason: This is the base case. Small memecoins seldom get 10-100x in one quarter without a new cycle-wide mania.
ANSEM is an influencer-named pump.fun token. Solana has thousands of these, and they usually peak early and fade, with attention spread across many rivals.
NetNet trades on a young Robinhood Chain with little on-chain liquidity or bridged capital. A $1B FDV there would need the whole ecosystem to take off first.
Cash Cat has the same Robinhood Chain liquidity limits. Even if the chain had a meme season, the gains would be split among several competing tokens, so any one is unlikely to reach $1B first.

failure_narrative: The basket loses in a reflexive Q4 2026 memecoin mania. Bitcoin and SOL break to new highs, and Robinhood adds on-chain features, token listings or app integrations that send its large retail base into Robinhood Chain memecoins. One chain meme, or ANSEM riding a Solana/pump.fun frenzy and influencer promotion, goes vertical. Its CoinGecko or CoinMarketCap FDV then prints at or above $1B, even for a minute. A thin-liquidity spike or an aggregator pricing glitch counts under the 'momentary crossing' rule. C5 and three of the four NO legs lose together. At most one NO leg survives: the winning coin's NO leg loses, while the NO legs on the coins that did not win still pay.
hedge_thesis: The basket fails only if risk appetite for speculative crypto surges into year-end. That means strong inflows to Bitcoin and Solana, a Robinhood Chain activity boom, and more retail trading. Those same conditions lift Robinhood's (HOOD) crypto trading revenue and stock price. They also lift SOL's price and pump.fun activity, and they push up Coinbase (COIN) volumes and speculative-asset beta. Instruments that go long crypto beta or Robinhood equity pay off in exactly the worlds where some memecoin reaches $1B FDV. When risk appetite is weak, they underperform, and in those worlds the primary wins.
